  rds: "../inst/extdata/cross_language.rds"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4)
res <- readRDS(params$rds)
```

Both packages fitted the same simulated data sets with the same cross-validation
folds (R generates both; pyfgls `r res$designs[[1]]$pyfgls`, fgls
`r res$fgls_version`, `r res$created`). Deterministic quantities are expected to
agree to machine precision; a few data sets can differ in the Lasso support when
the pyfgls Lasso path is inexact (penalties below float32 epsilon; see the
package documentation).

## Discrepancies by design and quantity

`max_abs` / `median_abs`: absolute differences; `max_rel`: largest relative
difference; `share_different`: share of data sets with a relative difference
above 1e-6 (or a different selected set / order).

```{r}
s <- res$summary
s$max_abs <- signif(s$max_abs, 3)
s$median_abs <- signif(s$median_abs, 3)
s$max_rel <- signif(s$max_rel, 3)
s$share_different <- round(s$share_different, 4)
knitr::kable(s, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Coverage of 95% intervals for the slope

```{r}
cv <- t(sapply(res$designs, function(d) d$coverage))
knitr::kable(round(cv, 4))
```

## Estimates and standard errors, R against Python

```{r, fig.height = 2.6 * ceiling(length(res$designs) / 2)}
op <- par(mfrow = c(length(res$designs), 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (nm in names(res$designs)) {
  d <- res$designs[[nm]]
  plot(d$py$beta, d$r$beta, pch = 20, cex = 0.5, xlab = "pyfgls", ylab = "fgls",
       main = paste(nm, "slope"))
  abline(0, 1, col = "grey")
  plot(d$py$se, d$r$se, pch = 20, cex = 0.5, xlab = "pyfgls", ylab = "fgls",
       main = paste(nm, "std. error"))
  abline(0, 1, col = "grey")
}
par(op)
```
